content: Hello. In the future gone be or there's any plan to increase the capabilities of the compiler for AVX, AVX2 and AVX512 instructions or it's better to maintain in a platform specific way. Because for parsing and specific checksum and other algorithm are benefit of that. Thank you for the help.
@RLC, are you looking for something like this?

notramo said in #beginners > Doubt about SIMD availability:

https://www.roc-lang.org/docs/main/Num/#U8x16

that's 128 bit register it's from the SSE instruction set. AVX, AVX2 have 256 bit if implemented should look something like U8x32 and U8x64 in the AVX512 standard

I kinda need registers as big as my CPU can handle. The why im asking it's cause im making a simd csv parser (for the love of the game) and kinda need that big registers for handling as many data as possible in every iteration.
I don't know whether it will be available in future versions.
I recommend writing your parsers with the U8x16 type, because the logic is the same.
And if wider SIMD support is added later, you can simply do a find-and-replace in your code.
The future is scalable vector length anyways. Dynamically select at runtime, instead of hardcoding into the codebase.

notramo said:

I recommend writing your parsers with the U8x16 type, because the logic is the same.

that's what i'm doing already. The edge cases gone be the same even with wider registers. But isn't just for wider registers too there's some algebraic operations that can be useful in detection of edge cases using bitmasking. thank you
